mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when GDPC1 YoY change is below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with deflationary pressure, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL < 1% for two months
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with deflation risk
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL < 1% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in real personal income (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which precedes tighter monetary policy and profit margin compression, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when UNRATE is below 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) during five consecutive months of HOUST above its 12-month moving average.
